source_review.notes: Checked six primary/official sources. Google Research supports tail amplification and tail-tolerant techniques at scale; Google SRE supports distribution/percentile rather than average latency measurement. gRPC supports one-deadline delayed hedging, max attempts, nonfatal statuses, cancellation, throttling, and pushback. AWS supports timeout/retry/idempotency/load cautions. Envoy documents overlapping hedge behavior on per-try timeout. Product mechanisms remain scoped and the independence model is explicitly conditional.

evidence: Checked branch latency X_i/CDF F_i, maximum M_n, exceedance p, concurrency C, fan-out F, attempts A, deadline D/reserve R, hedge unfinished fraction H, and orphan work W_o for consistent scopes.
Confirmed all-of uses a maximum/order statistic while sequential levels add elapsed time.
Confirmed expected hedge-rate notation is labeled approximate and paired with an absolute budget.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Independence is never presented as an incident safety guarantee.

evidence: Recomputed 1-0.99^100 as approximately 63.4% and 0.99^10 as approximately 90.4% (9.6% exceedance).
Recomputed 120 branches/20 concurrency as six waves and six times 40 ms as an idealized 240 ms.
Recomputed 50 parents times 12 branches as 600 and three attempts as 1,800 deepest attempts.
Recomputed 500-60-20-40 as 380 ms child execution, 100,000/s times 5% as 5,000 hedges/s, 1-0.98^40 as 55.4%, and 1-0.98^10 as 18.3%; counted ten examples and five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Wave and hedge calculations are scenarios; tails, queueing, correlation, and cancellation alter realized results.

evidence: Derived P(max X_i<=t)=product F_i(t), reducing to F(t)^n for identical independent branches.
Derived PC scoped in-flight bound and identified hidden retries, hedges, and nested fan-out as counterexamples.
Derived lambda*H approximate one-hedge rate and constructed correlated-pause case where H approaches one.
Confirmed early completion requires unobserved branches to be result-irrelevant or explicitly optional.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Quorum correctness is intentionally not inferred from the order-statistic formula.

evidence: Reviewed one/ten/hundred/unbounded branches, heterogeneous distributions, independent/perfect/mixed correlation, sequential layers, queue delay, merge/output cost, and deadline infeasibility.
Reviewed hot shard/key, host/zone/region/deployment/GC/common database, overload, cache miss, cold start, and recovery correlation.
Reviewed required/optional/substitutable/quorum/top-K semantics, inconsistent replicas, membership/epoch/authority, read-after-write/session token, and fatal/nonfatal status.

Reviewed cancellation at queue/send/execution/response/post-commit, late callback, orphan work, unsafe effects, same-host hedge, forged cardinality/priority, tenant unfairness, and cross-region policy.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans probability, resources, semantics, topology, security, cancellation, overload, and recovery.

evidence: Confirmed every parent has one deadline and bounded branch/concurrency/cost/attempt budgets.
Confirmed completion rule is declared before execution and early termination has semantic proof.
Confirmed children preserve merge/response reserves and queued infeasible work is not launched.
Confirmed cancellation releases local resources but is not treated as rollback or proof of remote stop.
Confirmed hedges use stable identity, eligible diverse destinations, aggregate throttling, and overload suppression.
invariant_checking.notes: Logical calls, branches, attempts, winners, losers, and orphan completions remain distinct.

evidence: Reviewed all-of amplification and confirmed independence/capacity limitations are explicit.
Reviewed fan-out load bound and confirmed its governed-scope assumptions.
Reviewed hedge-load estimate and confirmed absolute token/concurrency protection is still required.
Reviewed early-completion correctness and confirmed latency cannot override required result semantics.
proof_review.notes: No fastest-response or k-of-n policy is claimed to manufacture replica consistency.

evidence: Confirmed four arguments are labeled and assumptions/counterexamples are adjacent.
Confirmed Google Research/SRE, gRPC, AWS, and Envoy behavior is attributed to source scope.
Confirmed example percentile thresholds, reserves, concurrency, and token rates are policies to validate rather than standards.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mathematical estimates, product semantics, and empirical obligations are separated.

evidence: All six primary/official references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All branch counts, probabilities, delays, concurrency, deadlines, attempt factors, call rates, and hedge fractions are labeled scenarios.

Actual branch distributions/correlation, queue/service split, safe concurrency, hedge spare capacity, endpoint diversity, cancellation effectiveness, merge cost, consistency, and overload/recovery remain explicit trace/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production call graph, service mesh, replica set, or traffic distribution was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed completion rules, order statistics/correlation, cardinality and concurrency, deadlines/queues, stragglers, quorum consistency, cancellation, hedging, destination/result safety, aggregation, observability, and fault testing as one fan-out control model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through branch inventories, propagated budgets, per-parent/shared permits, completion-aware scheduling, stable identity, atomic winner state, delayed fleet-throttled hedges, topology eligibility, critical-path traces, orphan metrics, and independent/correlated load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module moves from order-statistic intuition through bounded execution and deadlines, then semantics, cancellation, hedging, aggregation, observation, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
